key_insight: AlB₁₂–Al detonation coatings improved the wear resistance of steel 45, with AB70 showing more stable tribological behavior.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer a potential wear-resistant surface treatment for steel components operating under sliding friction.
method: Deposited AB70 (70 wt.% AlB₁₂, 30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (30 wt.% AlB₁₂, 70 wt.% Al) using DNEPR-5M.
Characterized coating thickness, hardness, and surface structure.
Evaluated friction and wear under varying sliding speeds and loads.
evidence_signal: Coatings were approximately 170–200 μm thick; AB70 exhibited friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38 and wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km, with coated samples outperforming uncoated steel 45.
watch_item: Oxidative and adhesive-abrasive wear depended on friction conditions; the abstract does not specify operating ranges or quantify the improvement over uncoated steel.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
